previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system B-cell lymphoma was admitted electively for his 27th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. Admission labs revealed a persistently low white blood cell count (2.7), which contraindicated chemotherapy due to infection risk. The cause was unclear but likely related to prior treatment or possible bone marrow involvement. He remained on Keppra for seizure control and was started on lamotrigine for improved prophylaxis. Airborne precautions were initiated due to a positive PPD and family history of TB but discontinued after a chest X-ray showed only old granulomatous changes without active disease. He was discharged home with instructions to continue all home medications, monitor for rash on lamotrigine, and attend an outpatient bone marrow biopsy to evaluate the cause of leukopenia before resuming chemotherapy.

FINDINGS: 
BACKGROUND: Waking background is characterized by a 10 Hz alpha 
rhythm which attenuates with eye opening. Alpha rhythm amplitude 
is significantly higher over the right hemisphere. There is 
overall increased amplitude and accentuation of faster 
frequencies over the left hemisphere. There is mild intermittent 
focal slowing in the left centrotemporal region. 
HYPERVENTILATION: Is not performed secondary to the history of 
brain tumor. 
INTERMITTENT PHOTIC STIMULATION: Stepped photic stimulation from 
___ flashes per second (fps) produces no activation of the 
record. 
SLEEP: During brief drowsiness, the alpha rhythm attenuates and 
___ Hz slow waves appear diffusely followed by symmetric vertex 
waves. Stage II sleep is not recorded. 
CARDIAC MONITOR: A single EKG channel shows a generally regular 
rhythm with an average rate of 60-70 bpm. 
IMPRESSION: This is an abnormal awake and drowsy EEG because of 
mild 
intermittent focal slowing over the left central temporal region 
indicative of mild focal cerebral dysfunction in this region. 
Increased amplitude and accentuation of faster frequencies over 
the left hemisphere is consistent with breach artifact due to 
the known skull defect. No epileptiform discharges are present, 
but stage II sleep is not recorded. If clinically indicated, 
repeat EEG with sleep recording may provide additional 
information.
